previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and a history of recurrent diabetic foot ulcers was admitted for hyperglycemia with blood glucose over 500. The elevated sugars were attributed to a worsening left calcaneal osteomyelitis. She was not in DKA, and her blood sugar responded well to insulin. She underwent hemodialysis for volume overload, which improved her respiratory status and heart failure symptoms. Her sodium, which was initially low, normalized with fluid restriction. Antibiotics were briefly adjusted but reverted to her home regimen of vancomycin and ceftazidime per her preference. She was deemed a high-risk candidate for her upcoming below-the-knee amputation and advised to seek cardiology clearance. She was discharged home with services, continuing her insulin, antibiotics with dialysis, and all other home medications except gabapentin, which was discontinued.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ was admitted on ___ for cardiac optimization 
prior to her left BKA on ___ for a chronic non-healing 
calcaneal wound. She was started on Vancomycin and Ceftazadime 
for surgical prophylaxis. Pre-operative clearance included a 
___ P-MIBI which showed no evidence of cardiac ischemia. 
Per cardiology, atorvastatin 80 mg daily was started, lisinopril 
increased to 20 mg daily and Imdur and hydralazine were 
discontinued. She underwent two cycles of hemodialysis ___ 
and ___ prior to her surgery.   

On ___ she underwent a left below-the-knee amputation without 
complication.  Femoral and popliteal nerve catheters were placed 
pre-op for pain control following surgery. Popliteal and femoral 
nerve catheters were removed ___ and pain was well controlled 
on PO Dilaudid with intermittent IV dilaudid required only a few 
days post-operatively. She was started on a fentanyl patch for 
post-operative pain which should be weaned after her discharge. 
This summary is to be sent to Dr. ___ patient's PCP so 
that the patient does undergo withdrawl. 

During her hospitalization she continued to receive hemodialysis 
on her regular schedule. She has a history of urinary retention 
and required straight catheterization for 350cc on ___. Her 
Foley catheter has been discontinued. 

Warfarin was not started due to a history of calciphylaxis. 
Similarly she had a history of HIT, and was thus started on 
apixiban 5 mg twice daily 48 hours after her surgery, per 
cardiology recommendations. One dose was held for removal of her 
popliteal and femoral nerve catheters. She is discharged on 
apixiban 5mg BID for continued anticoagulation.

Vacomycin was continued. She should continue Vancomycin and 
Cefrazadine with each HD per HD protocol for 2 weeks or until 
changed otherwise before follow up with vascular surgery ___. Otherwise her incision is intact and clean and she had

Discharge Disposition:
Extended Care
 
Facility:
___
 
Discharge Diagnosis:
Severe peripheral vascular disease status post left below the 
knee amputation

 
Discharge Condition:
Mental Status: Clear and coherent.
Level of Consciousness: Alert and interactive.
Activity Status: Out of Bed with assistance to chair or 
wheelchair.

 
Discharge Instructions:
Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.

 On the side of your amputation you are non weight bearing for 
___ weeks. 
 You should keep this amputation site elevated when ever 
possible. 
 You may use the opposite foot for transfers and pivots.
 No driving until cleared by your Surgeon.
 No heavy lifting greater than 20 pounds for the next 3 weeks. 
BATHING/SHOWERING: 
 You may shower when you get home
 No tub baths or pools / do not soak your foot for 4 weeks from 
your date of surgery 
WOUND CARE:
 Sutures / Staples may have been removed before discharge. If 
they are not, an appointment will be made for you to return for 
staple removal. 
 When the sutures are removed the doctor may or may not place 
pieces of tape called steri-strips over the incision. These will 
stay on about a week and you may shower with them on. If these 
do not fall off after 10 days, you may peel them off with warm 
water and soap in the shower.
CAUTIONS:
 If you smoke, please make every attempt to quit.  Your primary 
care physician can help with this.  Smoking causes narrowing of 
your blood vessels which in turn decreases circulation.  
DIET:
 Low fat, low cholesterol / if you are diabetic  follow your 
dietary restrictions as before 
CALL THE OFFICE FOR: ___
 Bleeding, redness of, or drainage from your foot wound
 New pain, numbness or discoloration of the skin on the 
effected foot
 Fever greater than 101 degrees, chills, increased redness, or 
pus draining from the incision site
